name: Aggressive Playing 3-4-3

slots.why: The sweeper keeper covers the high space behind the three defenders.
The ball-playing stopper steps into duels and carries the ball into midfield when space opens.
The ball-playing cover defender sweeps behind the press and begins the next attack calmly.
The remaining defender provides a stable passing outlet beside the stopper-cover pair.
The attacking wing-back supplies the left-side width of the five-lane attack.
The right wing-back mirrors the aggressive width on the other side.
The box-to-box midfielder supports the press and arrives around the box.
The deep-lying playmaker connects the back three to the forward line.
The winger holds the left lane while the wing-back overlaps underneath.
The inside forward attacks the box from the right.
The pressing forward starts the press and leads the runs beyond the defence.

description: A high-line 3-4-3 that pairs an aggressive ball-playing stopper with a ball-playing cover defender and attacks through wing-backs.
whyGood: It offers an actual tactical home to proactive centre-backs who can both defend forward and progress possession.
whyThisShape: The stopper attacks the first duel, the cover defender protects behind him, and the third defender keeps the build-up stable. Wing-backs create the width while the front three press and occupy the final line.
whenToUse: When your centre-backs are quick, brave and technically secure, and you want to dominate territory with a back three.
whenNotToUse: Against quick direct counters if the cover defender lacks pace or the wing-backs cannot recover.

instructionRationale.Much Higher Line of Engagement: Begin pressure close to the opposition build-up and goalkeeper.
instructionRationale.Higher Defensive Line: Move the back line up to reduce the space behind the midfield and support territorial pressure.
instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Use the short connections supplied by the selected midfield and supporting forwards.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: Use short first-line outlets and midfield connections to start attacks; this asks for secure decisions under pressure.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Challenge immediately after losing possession, with the roles around the ball supporting the first pressure.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Centre Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.More Urgent Pressing: Challenge more often inside the selected engagement zone without making the settled press maximal.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Short Kicks: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
